pr_title: stardoc: auto-dedent rule doc and attribute docs
pr_body:
Makes them suitable for markdown output.

Fixes #13402
pr_comments: FYI @c-parsons could use someone's help to review/merge :)

Yeah I considered changing the existing DocstringParser class, but of course it has a bunch of fields which are specific to docs with structured sections like `Args:` and therefore it's probably a bigger change than this. More work to write and more work to review - and given how PRs often don't find anyone with time to review/merge them I didn't want to do all that work up front.

It's also somewhat risky to make deep changes to existing code, but the test coverage here is pretty good so I think the main issue is just author/reviewer time.
My question for @tetromino is whether you have time to review a big refactoring here and if that's what you want, before I spend time digging in to how is could be done.
@tetromino I think the ball is still in your court, I don't want to invest in a refactoring here that doesn't get merged

issue_context.title: Typical formatting of rule docstring is unusable for Markdown output
issue_context.body:
Commonly a rule with multi-line documentation can have a second paragraph, which developers commonly indent to be readable within the dictionary where it's declared:

```
example_rule = rule(
    implementation = _rule_impl,
    doc = """Small example of rule using a markdown template.

    This paragraph should not have extra intent, as that would make it a code block.
    """,
    attrs = {
        "first": attr.string(doc = "This is the first attribute"),
        "second": attr.string(default = "2"),
    },
)
```

However when producing Markdown-format output, the extra indent on the lines following the first causes that text to be a code block.

> Small example of rule using a markdown template.
> ```
>     This paragraph should not have extra intent, as that would make it a code block.
> ```

Bazel has [code to account for this](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/4.0.0/src/tools/starlark/java/com/google/devtools/starlark/common/DocstringUtils.java#L202) by inferring the baseline indentation, however this logic doesn't apply to the rule documentation string.

As a real-world example, see the codeblock that appears here:
https://bazelbuild.github.io/rules_kotlin/kotlin#kt_jvm_binary
and the (ugly) fix required currently:
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_kotlin/pull/533/files#diff-4494836edf6b3f0b67056cb72ef24752d21a8c08eb8f2ca4790780179dd76d81R315
comments: The same problem can be observed on docstrings for rule attributes. I can file a separate issue for that if the fixes go in separate PRs.

@tetromino and I agree that this is useful for markdown and seems at least non-harmful for other output formats.

If we already have indentation logic, we should probably share it for any built-in dedent feature. But we could consider making a (backwards incompatible) change if that logic is surprising/deficient.

Design questions:

* What strategy should dedent logic use? Python has [`textwrap.dedent`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/textwrap.html#textwrap.dedent), but that doesn't account for the first line, which is often unindented non-whitespace content. It also doesn't strip leading and trailing whitespace/newlines, which arguably you might want in order to treat

```
    def f():
        """
        abc
        xyz
        """
```

as identical to

```
    def f():
        """abc
        xyz"""
```

* What should be considered whitespace? `textwrap.dedent` handles both spaces and tabs but considers them non-equal for the purpose of determining common leading whitespace. Should we do the same? But Starlark (at least the Java implementation) doesn't allow tabs for indentation of code, so allowing it for documentation seems inconsistent.

* Where in the pipeline should indentation processing be applied?

    * Immediately upon evaluation of the docstring (e.g. `StarlarkFunction#getDocumentation`)? This would mean indentation is already processed (and not recoverable) at the time of a hypothetical `bazel query` command that dumped out doc content.

    * Before generating the doc content protos (`stardoc_output.proto`)? But note that when we rewrite stardoc doc extraction, this choice kind of merges with the above.

    * Internally to whatever rendering template applies to the extracted doc content?
https://github.com/bazelbuild/stardoc/pull/170 will complete the fix by updating Stardoc's extractor

review_comments: Why never dedent the first line? Note that you do use the first line for calculating `indentation` if the first line's indentation level is non-zero.

Returning `doc` unchanged on line 110 implies that all-whitespace lines become empty lines (even if they contain whitespace beyond `indentation`) if any dedentation is done, but remain unchanged when not dedenting - which is unintuitive behavior.

Would it make more sense to instead dedent all-whitespace lines by up to the same number of spaces as any other line?
`line.trim()` removes tabs (as well as all other characters below 0x20, e.g. windows carriage returns), not just spaces. `DocstringParser.getIndentation()` counts only spaces.

This is true, but it points out a design problem. It is completely unscalable to allow different formats for the content of the docstring. Producing a unified doc set and/or pre-rendering the doc in a PR review becomes a guessing game of pick the right render engine. We should insist on markdown, or html, or anything, as long as the rendering rules for it are well defined.

That ship sailed a long time ago I think. There are several old stardoc issues about it.

For this context we can just say "let's not introduce leading white space to accept as many inputs as possible"

Actually. The comment is probably fine.  I was just grumbling. I'm totally in favor of this CL.

But to be honest, I am going to propose that for rules to play together well - in terms of mixing them all into a unified doc set - that we pick a single markup syntax and start converging toward that.  But we don't have to make that choice at the stardoc level. It is something that should come from the overall project and push down.
